experiment: Experiment 1 -- block transfer by LoRa radio between two machines
why: +5V and 3V3 are adjacent on the CP2102 header. 5 V destroys an RYLR998 and there is no spare, so this is the step with no undo. Recorded before the modules were attached, because a measurement written down afterwards is a recollection rather than evidence.
instrument: Themisto TH-M100 AC/DC True RMS digital multimeter, 6000 counts, 10 A, CAT III 600 V. DC volts, red lead in the V/ohm/mA socket.
method: black probe on GND (pin 5 counting from the DTR end), red on pin 6 (3V3) then pin 4 (+5V). BOTH rails measured deliberately: a single 3.3 V reading cannot distinguish the correct pin from a miscount, whereas 3.3 on pin 6 AND 5.0 on pin 4 confirms the pin identification itself.
rylr998_tolerance: 3.3 V nominal, headroom to about 3.6 V; both rails are comfortably inside spec and the two agree within 27 mV

instrument_identification.how: Identified on 2026-09-27 from photographs of the meter, and confirmed by the operator.
instrument_identification.why_it_is_recorded_this_way: The original entry said only 'handheld multimeter', which is unattributable: a reader cannot judge whether 3.369 V carries three meaningful decimals without knowing the instrument. At 6000 counts a 6 V range resolves 1 mV, so three decimals sit inside its resolution.
instrument_identification.the_honest_limit: The photographs postdate the measurement by three weeks. That this is the same meter rests on the operator's confirmation, not on anything recorded at the bench on 2026-09-06. The readings themselves are unchanged.
